questions.q_en: If P @ Q means that P is mother-in-law of Q, P % Q means that P is mother of Q, P * Q means P is the daughter of Q and P $ Q means that P is the son of Q, then which of the following expression shows that A is the granddaughter of G?
questions.solution_en:
It is given that,

P @ Q means that P is mother-in-law of Q,

P % Q means that P is mother of Q,

P * Q means P is the daughter of Q,

P $ Q means that P is the son of Q.

Option (a) A @ D $ F $ G

A is the mother-in-law of D. D is the son of F and F is the son of G.

Here, A is not the granddaughter of G.

Option (b) A * R $ G

A is the daughter of R and R is the son of G.

Here, A is the granddaughter of G.

Option (c) A % S @ G

A is the mother of S and S is the mother-in-law of G.

Here, A is not the granddaughter of G.

Option (d) A * J % G

A is the daughter of J and J is the mother of G.

Here, A is not the granddaughter of G.

P % Q means that P is mother of Q,

questions.q_en: If 31 December 2003 was a Wednesday, then what was the day of the week on 7 March 2005?
questions.solution_en:
31 December 2003 was the last day in 2003 and 2004 was the leap year which means 2004 had 366 days.

Jan had 31 days, Feb has 28 days, and from 1st march to 7th march total days = 7

Hence, total days from 1 Jan 2004 to 7 Mar 2005 = 366 + 31 + 28 + 7 = 432 days = 61 weeks and 5 days.

Since, 30 Dec 2003 was a Wednesday which means 7 Mar 2005 was 5th days after Thursday.

5th day after Wednesday is Monday.

Hence, 7 March 2005 was a Monday.
questions.solution_hi:

Jan had 31 days, Feb has 28 days, and from 1st march to 7th march total days = 7

Hence, total days from 1 Jan 2004 to 7 Mar 2005 = 366 + 31 + 28 + 7 = 432 days = 61 weeks and 5 days.

Since, 30 Dec 2003 was a Wednesday which means 7 Mar 2005 was 5th days after Thursday.

5th day after Wednesday is Monday.

Hence, 7 March 2005 was a Monday.

questions.q_en:
A question is given, followed by two statements labelled I and II. Identify which of the statements is/are sufficient to answer the question.

Question:

Five houses of five different colours (blue, green, yellow, red and violet), with equal space between every two adjacent houses, are constructed in a row facing north. Which coloured house is exactly in the middle of the row?

Statements:

(I) Green and yellow coloured houses are constructed at the extreme ends of the row.

(II) Violet and blue coloured houses are immediate neighbouring houses of green and yellow coloured houses, respectively.
options_en: Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not
Data in Statements I and II together is not sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not
Data in Statements I and II together is sufficient to answer the question
questions.solution_en:
Five houses of five different colours (blue, green, yellow, red and violet), with equal space between every two adjacent houses, are constructed in a row facing north.

Only statement I:

(I) Green and yellow coloured houses are constructed at the extreme ends of the row.

So, which coloured house is exactly in the middle of the row is unknown.

Only statement II:

(II) Violet and blue coloured houses are immediate neighbouring houses of green and yellow coloured houses, respectively.

So, which coloured house is exactly in the middle of the row is unknown.

Both statement I and II:

(I) Green and yellow coloured houses are constructed at the extreme ends of the row

(II) Violet and blue coloured houses are immediate neighbouring houses of green and yellow coloured houses, respectively

So, Red coloured house is exactly in the middle of the row.

Thus, Data in Statements I and II together is sufficient to answer the question.
